column1: # THE BOOTSTRAP WORK PACKAGES. Source-derived bounded packages, NOT
# Each package names the source set it owns, the gate it must
# satisfy, the smallest runnable witness that discharges it, and its
# ACT cost with an EXPLICIT cost basis. Every cost basis names the
# cohort the number came from, or declares the range JUDGEMENTAL.
# The dependency edges are in c2/work-package-dependencies.tsv.

column4: goal
column10: owned_semantics
column11: smallest_runnable_witness
column16: cost_basis
column19: reason

column4: PolyC-authored driver: argument parsing and the compile entry point
column10: argument handling and the dispatch into the compile pipeline
column11: hcc --install-dir=X -c input.HC -o out.o emits a compiler artifact
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the 9 historical parser implementation ACTs were 1 site per ACT; a driver is 2-3 sites of the same kind
column19: THE EARLIEST GATE: without a PolyC-authored driver there is no compiler-producing precursor, so every other package is unreachable

column4: PolyC-authored compile pipeline: read file, lex, parse, emit
column10: the compileToAst/compileToAsm pipeline and the control-symbol state
column11: a PolyC-authored compileToAsm emits assembly text for a representative source
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: 9 parser decisions took 9 implementation ACTs at 1 site per ACT; the pipeline owns 5 sites of comparable kind
column19: the pipeline is the SECOND step of the precursor and binds the lexer and parser together

column4: PolyC-authored lexer producing the token stream
column10: the token classification and the trivia/scan decisions
column11: a PolyC-authored lexer reproduces the token sequence of a representative source
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the 9 historical parser slices are the closest cohort (9 ACTs for 9 sites); the lexer owns 7 sites of comparable kind, so the observed 1-site-per-ACT floor is 7
column19: the lexer is the FIRST semantic subsystem the precursor needs, and 6 of its sites already have dormant PolyC prototypes that are selector-OFF today

column4: PolyC-authored parser and AST construction
column10: the recursive-descent decisions and the AST node construction
column11: a PolyC-authored parser builds an AST for a representative source
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: 9 historical parser implementation ACTs for 9 sites; the parser owns 8 sites of comparable kind, so the observed floor is 8
column19: nine parser decisions are ALREADY PolyC-authored; this package is the boundary DEFINITION and the remaining parser surface, not a from-scratch rewrite

column4: PolyC-authored AST node construction and the type/state transitions
column10: the AST node kinds and the ast.h layout contract
column11: a PolyC-authored AST builder produces the node kinds the codegen consumes
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the AST is a stateful module and the 9-site parser cohort does NOT transfer; the range is declared, NOT measured
column19: the AST layout is the TYPE_REPRESENTATION dependency that 95 of the 135 graph edges observe; it is the deepest cut in the whole programme

column4: PolyC-authored string and container primitives
column10: the AoStr growth and the container ownership rules
column11: a PolyC-authored AoStr passes the string growth cases
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the 9-site parser cohort at 1 site per ACT gives a floor of 3
column19: the containers are a hard prerequisite of every other package and are pure, so they are the cheapest real work in the programme

column4: PolyC-authored IR construction and the neutral-boundary contract
column10: the IR opcode set and the neutral parameter/physical register split
column11: a PolyC-authored IR builder produces the opcodes the backend consumes
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort exists for a neutral-boundary module; the range is declared, NOT measured
column19: the IR is the module the earlier IR-BOUNDARY02 regression lived in, so its risk is measured to be higher than a pure module

column4: PolyC-authored CFG construction and the recovery/dominance rules
column10: the dominance and the recovery-point representation
column11: a PolyC-authored CFG builder produces the blocks the backend consumes
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort; the recovery edge class (12 edges) is a known risk area
column19: the CFG carries the RECOVERY obligation, one of the three edge classes with a runtime proof requirement

column4: PolyC-authored assembly emission and the instruction printer
column10: the instruction encoding and the format strings
column11: a PolyC-authored assembler emits the expected assembly text for a fixture
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort for the assembler
column19: the assembler is the narrowest real COMPILER OUTPUT, so it is the smallest unit that can discharge the P0 real-compiler-output predicate on its own

column4: PolyC-authored AArch64 backend
column10: the condition-code selection and the register allocation contract
column11: a PolyC-authored AArch64 backend emits the expected assembly for a fixture
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the backend is the largest single semantic unit and 2 of its decision sites are ALREADY PolyC-authored, which is evidence the unit is tractable
column19: the backend owns the two migrated A64 condition decisions, so it is the unit with the most existing PolyC precedent

column4: PolyC-authored x86-64 backend
column10: the x86-64 register allocation and the legacy AST backend
column11: a PolyC-authored x86-64 backend emits the expected assembly for a fixture
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort; 6544 LOC across the two units
column19: the x86-64 backend is NOT on the host-target critical path, so it can proceed in parallel with the AArch64 backend

column4: PolyC-authored JSON emitter
column10: the JSON value model
column11: a PolyC-authored JSON emitter reproduces the fixture output
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: 19 authority rows and 378 LOC make this a small unit
column19: JSON is not on the M2 path, so it is deliberately LAST in the M2 ordering

column4: PolyC-authored language server
column10: the LSP request/response model
column11: a PolyC-authored LSP responds to a request fixture
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort; 2134 LOC
column19: the LSP is a tool surface, not a compiler-producing path

column4: PolyC-authored REPL
column10: the REPL evaluation loop
column11: a PolyC-authored REPL evaluates a fixture expression
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort; 1568 LOC
column19: the REPL is a tool surface, not a compiler-producing path

column4: PolyC-authored C-to-PolyC transpiler
column10: the C-to-PolyC source mapping
column11: a PolyC-authored transpiler produces the expected output for a C fixture
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort; 1747 LOC
column19: the transpiler is a migration ACCELERATOR, not a compiler-producing path

column4: PolyC-authored memory-safety checker
column10: the memory-safety rules
column11: a PolyC-authored checker accepts or rejects the fixture
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: no historical cohort; 328 LOC
column19: a small analyser, not on the M2 path

column4: PolyC-authored ABI and shared-state foundation for the compiler source set
column10: the shared ABI between the PolyC modules
column11: a PolyC-authored ABI contract compiles two modules against each other
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the archived forecast assumed 3 ACTs for the programme ABI foundation; the range 2/4/8 brackets that assumption
column19: the shared ABI is the coupling that makes the 19-component SCC a REAL migration constraint, and it must be settled before the parts can move independently

column4: Production generation and qualification of the precursor compiler
column10: the producer provenance of the precursor
column11: a qualified earlier compiler compiles the precursor source set and the precursor runs
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the archived forecast assumed 10 ACTs for M2 bootstrap; this package covers only the PRECURSOR generation
column19: this is the package that turns a source set into a COMPILER PRODUCING artifact; without it P0 stays BLOCKED

column4: Correction and verification reserve for the whole M2 scope
column10: the differential witnesses and the regression suites
column11: NONE
column16: MEASURED_COHORT: the historical correction rate is 0.44 (4 correction ACTs per 9 implementation ACTs) measured on the PARSER cohort only; applied to a stateful compiler programme this is a LOWER bound
column19: the reserve is the transfer of a narrow parser-slice correction rate to stateful compiler modules, and it is the single largest judgemental assumption in the model

column4: Generation qualification of the FULL M2 source set and the M2 gate discharge
column10: the producer provenance of the complete compiler source set
column11: a qualified earlier compiler compiles the complete in-scope source set and the result runs
column16: JUDGEMENTAL: the archived forecast assumed 3 ACTs for the M2 generation harness
column19: this is the package that actually DISCHARGES the M2 gate; the predecessor packages only make it reachable
